scenes.goal: Earn curiosity through material evidence and conflicting needs.
scenes.obstacle: No usable firearm, trial, battle use or complete understanding.
scenes.intended_change: Earn access through a costly bargain and physical acquisition.
scenes.location: Achaean shore and smiths’ shelters after a storm
scenes.time: After a storm, a smith and Odysseus investigate a damaged divine object.

scenes.goal: Bind himself, conceal part of the price and bring back six weapons plus a fixed finite charge supply.
scenes.obstacle: Keeper must want something. No infinite supply.
scenes.intended_change: Earn access through a costly bargain and physical acquisition.
scenes.location: Concealed coastal sanctuary reached by a difficult journey
scenes.time: Odysseus binds himself, conceals part of the price and brings back six weapons plus a fixed finite charge supply.

scenes.goal: Establish every limitation used in the climax, maintain third-person epic language during practical work.
scenes.obstacle: No unanimous conversion by a speech. Establish every limitation used in the climax.
scenes.intended_change: Make possession a conflict over use, authority and who faces danger.
scenes.location: Secluded trial ground, then the Achaean council
scenes.time: A trial shows power and established failures; competing physical claims pursue different aims. Thestor learns that indispensable knowledge blocks departure.

scenes.goal: Local climax: constrained first deployment, costly choice, consequential aftermath.
scenes.obstacle: No massacre or fall of Troy. Mark any Trojan focal shift. End on a concrete obligation or action, not a moral explanation.
scenes.intended_change: Local climax: constrained first deployment, costly choice, consequential aftermath.
scenes.location: Contested approach between Greek defenses and Trojan fighting line
scenes.time: Achilles enters danger to protect operators he opposed. Thestor chooses between equipment and a dependent. Greeks secure the position; a specific irreversible loss follows an established limitation and human decision.

threads: What becomes of heroic honor when a man of little standing can strike down a champion beyond spear reach?
Loyalty to comrades versus obedience to a king
The discovery of the weapons leads to a crisis that forces the first constrained deployment
The keeper of the weapons wants something in return for the cache, creating a conflict over possession and conditions
The discovery makes him necessary and prevents departure
The bargain binds him to an obligation he cannot safely disclose
He sees the costs hidden in heroic boasting while concealing the costs of his own bargains
The weapons diminish the worth of the warrior
The weapons have visible material limits and imperfect aim
The weapons are described only enough to understand action and failure
